subject: Recap + next steps — Private VPC networking
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@finlytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps — Private VPC networking

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap so we’re aligned and so I can loop in our networking folks for the technical deep-dive.

Call summary:
- Primary ask: private, VPC-based deployment for inference (no public endpoints).
- Preference: FinLytics would prefer VPC peering if possible; Open to PrivateLink if it simplifies routing.
- Region: us-west-2 (primary).
- Expected steady-state: ~200 qps (spiky bursts up to ~500 qps), per-request payloads ~1–3KB.
- Data residency: customer data must stay in their VPC; control/management plane access required for health and metrics.
- Timeline: target pilot by end of Q2, production H2.

What we need from your network team:
1) Current VPC CIDR(s) and any overlapping ranges — you mentioned 10.10.0.0/16? Please confirm.
2) A network diagram showing subnets, NAT/gateway, firewall/egress rules.
3) Any org security constraints (no-peering with external accounts, must use PrivateLink, static IP allowlist only, etc.).

What we’ll provide from Redwood:
- Initial network requirements checklist (attached): redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf
- Example network diagram and suggested CIDR allocations: example-network-diagram.png (attached)
- Proposed AWS account IDs and short list of IP ranges for management/control plane so you can validate allowlists.

Proposed next steps:
- Share your network diagram and ACLs (attach to this thread) — FinLytics internal network lead on copy would be great.
- Schedule a 30-min technical call (Marissa + Sean + Dev engineer) with Raj/your cloud network lead to validate peering vs PrivateLink.
- Once we agree on connectivity pattern we’ll produce a scoped SOW/quote for Private deployment + reserved capacity.

Attaching: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf, example-network-diagram.png

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed time slots in a separate calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole

- We are leaning toward VPC peering (simpler for our infra team) unless Redwood recommends PrivateLink for security reasons.

Date: 2026-03-16T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Private VPC networking

Hi Alice / Raj — great, thanks for the diagram. Quick answers and a few technical details to help your network team evaluate:

Connectivity options (summary):
1) VPC peering (recommended if no CIDR overlap) — simple routing, lower ops surface.
2) AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) — recommended if you do not want cross-account peering or want to minimize routing table changes.
3) IP allowlist for control plane (management/metrics) — complementary; will still need network connectivity for data plane.

Typical network requirements (initial):
- Data plane (model inference): via peering — treat as intra-VPC routing; no public internet required.
- Control plane (health metrics, metrics ingestion, tracing): TLS 443 outbound to a small set of management endpoints — we’ll provide the IPs and AWS account IDs.
- Ports: primarily 443/TCP for encrypted API and control traffic. For peering, intra-VPC traffic uses standard ephemeral ports; no special ports required.
- NAT: if your subnets are private and have no outbound egress, you may need NAT for any outbound connections to our control plane endpoints unless you use PrivateLink.

Action items from our side: I’m attaching a file that lists the Redwood AWS account IDs and recommended ephemeral CIDRs for the deployment to avoid overlap: redwood-aws-ids.txt

Immediate next steps:
- Raj: can you confirm whether 10.10.0.0/16 overlaps with any other networks you plan to peer with? If not, VPC peering should be straightforward.
- If peering isn’t allowed, we’ll propose PrivateLink and share an interface endpoint configuration.
- Proposed tech call: Tue 2026-03-17 10:00-10:30 PDT or Wed 2026-03-17 15:00-15:30 PDT — which works best for Raj? I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Relevant links: HubSpot opportunity: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-2026-0412

Thanks — Sean and Dev are on copy and will handle the deep-dive on the call.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — quick technical Qs before the call:

1) NAT/egress: if we peer the VPCs, will FinLytics incur additional egress charges for inference traffic (i.e., will traffic traverse the public internet)? Our preference is to keep data within AWS networking to avoid egress costs.
2) IPs/account IDs: can you confirm how long the management IP list might change? We need stable IPs or a documented rotation window to automate firewall rules.
3) Encryption/metadata: any TLS termination or does the traffic remain end-to-end encrypted between our instances and Redwood? We need to ensure no plaintext payloads are sent through the control plane.

We can do the Tue 2026-03-17 10:00-10:30 PDT slot. Please send calendar invite.

-Raj
Cloud Network Lead | FinLytics
raj@finlytics.com
